question: One of the objectives under UN Sustainable Development Goal 3.3 is to get the HIV/AIDS epidemic under control by 2030. The latest progress report by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control from 20241 shows that only a few EU and EEA countries have achieved the targets. Will the Commission press for the Member States to commit to tracing unreported HIV infections and offering free, anonymous HIV tests?

According to a report entitled ‘Rapid Assessment on Access to PrEP in EU/EEA Countries’2, the options for obtaining PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis – prophylactic treatment to prevent HIV) within the EU/EEA countries vary widely. Will the Commission press for PrEP to be made available to the relevant target groups in all the Member States? In 2023, around 1.

3 million people were infected with HIV3 and around 630 000 died from AIDS-related diseases. Some 39.9 million people all over the world are living with HIV. The HIV epidemic is on the rise in Eastern Europe and Central Asia, where UNAIDS has reported that around 2.1 million people are living with HIV.
Will the Commission step up funding for global health, including by contributing to the Global Fund and the forthcoming framework programme for research and innovation?
Progress towards reaching the SDG 3.3 targets related to HIV, TB, viral hepatitis and STIs in the EU/EEA PrEp report final part 1 GAU-2024-Full-report_En.pdf
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2025) The organisation and delivery of health services and medical falls within the Member States’ responsibilities pursuant to Article 168(7) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. The EU supports Member States in various ways.

The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) recommends that Member States follow the clinical guidelines of the European AIDS Clinical Society on post-exposure prophylaxis for HIV1 and has issued guidance on testing policies2.

The ECDC collects and analyses data in cooperation with the World Health Organization producing annual reports and monitoring progresses against the Sustainable Development Goal 3.3. The Health Security Committee3 periodically reviews and discusses the progress and challenges in relation to the achievement of Goal 3.3.

The Commission has been a strong supporter of the Global Fund (GF) since its creation in 2002, most recently through the pledge made by the President in 2022 of EUR 715 million for the seventh replenishment cycle, which covers the grants for the period 2024-2026.

The Commission is aware of the GF’s eighth replenishment cycle and associated pledging events and is assessing options which are framed by current implementation levels of the multiannual financial framework.
